source_text: Μετὰ τὴν εἴσοδον εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ τὴν ἐκβολὴν τῶν πωλούντων ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ ζητοῦσιν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖ. Ὁ δὲ ἀντερωτᾷ περὶ τοῦ βαπτίσματος Ἰωάννου, καὶ ἐλέγχει τὴν ὑπόκρισιν τῶν μὴ θελόντων εἰπεῖν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων. Οὕτως ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ Λόγου φανερὰ γίνεται τοῖς καρποφοροῦσιν, κρύπτεται δὲ τοῖς φύλλα μόνον ἔχουσιν. Δόξα Χριστῷ. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The authority of the Word revealed to fruit-bearers
orientation: Origen is commenting on the events after Jesus enters the city and drives the sellers out of the temple, when the chief priests question his authority.
pass_a_gloss: After the entrance into the city and the casting out of the [ones] selling from the temple [they] seek the chief priests in what authority these [things] he does. The [one] but asks in return about the baptism of John, and [he] exposes the hypocrisy of the [ones] not willing to say from heaven or from men. Thus the authority of the Word manifest becomes to the [ones] bearing fruit, [it] is hidden but to the [ones] leaves only having. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary term for the authority by which Jesus acts, questioned by the chief priests.
The verb means to refute or expose, and the noun is the glossary term for pretense.
The participle is active and present, matching the fruit-bearing theme of the preceding section.
Echoes the fig tree with leaves but no fruit from the preceding section.

bible_refs.note: The chief priests ask in what authority Jesus does these things.
Jesus asks in return about the baptism of John, whether from heaven or from men.

pass_b_english: After the entrance into the city and the casting out of those selling from the temple, the chief priests ask in what authority he does these things (Matthew 21:23). But he asks in return about the baptism of John, and exposes the hypocrisy of those unwilling to say whether it was from heaven or from men (Matthew 21:25). In this way the authority of the Word becomes clear to those bearing fruit, but is hidden from those having only leaves. Glory to Christ. Amen.
